overview: Two names for the two DNA strands of a gene, defined by their relationship to the mRNA produced.
genZNote: Template strand is the strand actually read. Coding strand is the strand that looks just like the finished mRNA.

aspects.label: Role in Transcription
aspects.valueA: Physically read by RNA polymerase to synthesise mRNA.
aspects.valueB: Not read directly, but has the same sequence as the mRNA (with T instead of U).

aspects.label: Sequence Match to mRNA
aspects.valueB: Identical to the mRNA sequence, except thymine (T) replaces uracil (U).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: If you're given the coding strand sequence, you can read off the mRNA sequence directly by swapping T for U.
overlay.memoryTrick: Coding strand 'codes' the same message as mRNA. Template strand is the actual mould RNA polymerase uses.
overlay.commonMisconception: RNA polymerase does not read the coding strand — it's a common exam trap. It always reads the template strand.
